description:
pkix-ct/src/lib.rs:68 marks Error #[non_exhaustive] (good). But the public data structs:
- CtLog (log_list.rs:25) — likely to grow fields (mmd_seconds, log_type, dns API base, etc.)
- SctList (sct.rs:137) — newtype Vec<SCT>, low risk but still
- SignedCertificateTimestamp (sct.rs:56) — likely to grow if RFC 9162 v2 ever ships
- MerkleAuditPath (verify.rs:592) — could grow (e.g., explicit subtree_size for partial proofs)
- SignedTreeHead (verify.rs:568) — could grow

None of them carry #[non_exhaustive]. Adding any field becomes a breaking change to construction (pattern matching is unlikely on these but exhaustive construction is).

Per AGENTS.md prelaunch framing ('Design for the eventual complete shape', 'Breaking changes are free'): pre-1.0 the marker is cheap and removes a class of future breaking changes. Post-1.0 adding fields without the marker is breaking.

Pre-1.0 the practical cost is callers must use struct update syntax or .new() — both healthy. Suggested fix: add #[non_exhaustive] to each public struct that's expected to grow, and add a constructor (CtLog::new() / SignedCertificateTimestamp::new()) that takes all current fields and returns Self. Same shape as the workspace's existing TrustAnchor / ValidationPolicy non-exhaustive types.

Reference: PKIX-tit4.29 (Error::MalformedAnchor struct variant) is the same kind of finding in pkix-truststore; same fix applies here at struct level.
title: Public data structs (CtLog, SctList, SignedCertificateTimestamp, MerkleAuditPath, SignedTreeHead) lack #[non_exhaustive]
